answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by binding each identity to a slow-verifying hardware pulse beacon whose attested latency, cross-checked against asynchronous telemetry quorums, makes mass forgery costly. Consensus admits new agents only after a dawn-to-dusk cooling epoch, gating reputation behind a glacier-slow collateral escrow that penalizes abrupt identity bursts. Adversaries forging identities face an immediate O(k * S) capital forfeiture.
